description: HypoGuard AI - Indian Food Nutrition Database

foods.name: Chapati
foods.recommendation: Whole-wheat chapati is a balanced staple. Pair with dal and vegetables to keep the meal blood-sugar friendly.

foods.name: Phulka
foods.recommendation: Low-fat, roasted flatbread. Excellent daily choice; limit to 2 per meal.

foods.name: Paratha
foods.recommendation: High in fat from ghee/oil. Choose tawa-roasted versions and eat in moderation.

foods.name: Aloo Paratha
foods.recommendation: Potato stuffing raises carbs significantly. Best as a treat, pair with curd to slow absorption.

foods.name: Poori
foods.recommendation: Deep-fried, calorie-dense. Limit to 2-3 pieces occasionally.

foods.name: Bhatura
foods.recommendation: Refined-flour fried bread. High carb and fat; rare indulgence only.

foods.name: Naan
foods.recommendation: Refined flour raises blood sugar quickly. Prefer whole-wheat roti instead.

foods.name: White Rice
foods.recommendation: High glycemic load. Control portion to half a bowl or choose brown rice.

foods.name: Brown Rice
foods.recommendation: Higher fibre, lower GI than white rice. Great blood-sugar-friendly staple.

foods.name: Jeera Rice
foods.recommendation: Ghee adds calories. Keep portion moderate and combine with dal.

foods.name: Lemon Rice
foods.recommendation: Flavoured with oil and peanuts. Watch portion to manage carbs.

foods.name: Pulao
foods.recommendation: Veggie pulao adds fibre. Serve with raita to lower glycemic response.

foods.name: Khichdi
foods.recommendation: Rice + dal combo is gentle on blood sugar. Excellent for diabetic meals.

foods.name: Biryani
foods.recommendation: Calorie-dense and carb-heavy. Choose chicken biryani and limit to small portions.

foods.name: Curd Rice
foods.recommendation: Fermented curd slows digestion. Comforting and moderate for sugar levels.

foods.name: Dal Tadka
foods.recommendation: Excellent protein and low GI. Include dal in every meal for balanced nutrition.

foods.name: Moong Dal
foods.recommendation: Easily digestible, high protein. Great choice for diabetic-friendly diet.

foods.name: Masoor Dal
foods.recommendation: Red lentils, rich in fibre and low GI. Excellent everyday dal.

foods.name: Toor Dal
foods.recommendation: Staple dal with low glycemic impact. Pairs well with roti.

foods.name: Dal Makhani
foods.recommendation: Cream and butter raise fat. Request light version with less cream.

foods.name: Chana Dal
foods.recommendation: Split chickpeas are high in protein and fibre. Great for sugar control.

foods.name: Aloo Gobi
foods.recommendation: Cauliflower is great; potato raises carbs. Pair with more sabzi than rice.

foods.name: Bhindi
foods.recommendation: Low-carb okra, great for diabetic plates. High in fibre.

foods.name: Palak Paneer
foods.recommendation: Iron-rich spinach with paneer protein. Balanced and filling.

foods.name: Paneer Butter Masala
foods.recommendation: High fat from cream and butter. Enjoy occasionally in small portions.

foods.name: Mix Veg
foods.recommendation: Fibre-rich vegetable medley. Excellent daily accompaniment.

foods.name: Baingan Bharta
foods.recommendation: Roasted eggplant, smoky and low carb. Great diabetic option.

foods.name: Pumpkin Curry
foods.recommendation: Pumpkin is mildly sweet. Moderate portion keeps carbs in check.

foods.name: Bottle Gourd
foods.recommendation: Very low carb, high water content. Excellent for sugar management.

foods.name: Matar Paneer
foods.recommendation: Peas add fibre, paneer adds protein. Balanced meal option.

foods.name: Cabbage Sabzi
foods.recommendation: Cabbage is very low in carbs. Safe to eat generously.

foods.name: Cauliflower Sabzi
foods.recommendation: Low-carb cruciferous vegetable. Excellent for diabetic diet.

foods.name: Idli
foods.recommendation: Steamed and light. Pair with sambar for protein and fibre.

foods.name: Dosa
foods.recommendation: Fermented rice-lentil crepe. Choose without ghee and with sambar.

foods.name: Masala Dosa
foods.recommendation: Potato filling adds carbs. Share or choose plain dosa for lower carbs.

foods.name: Medu Vada
foods.recommendation: Deep-fried urad dal. High in fat; limit frequency.

foods.name: Uttapam
foods.recommendation: Veggie-topped pancake. Moderate GI, choose veggie-rich toppings.

foods.name: Sambar
foods.recommendation: Lentil-vegetable stew with low GI. Pairs perfectly with idli/dosa.

foods.name: Upma
foods.recommendation: Semolina is refined; control portion and add more vegetables.

foods.name: Pongal
foods.recommendation: Rice + moong dal. Moderate portion with ghee-reduced preparation.

foods.name: Poha
foods.recommendation: Flattened rice is moderate GI. Add peanuts and veggies for balance.

foods.name: Samosa
foods.recommendation: Fried and carb-dense. Occasional treat; limit to one.

foods.name: Kachori
foods.recommendation: Deep-fried and calorie-dense. Rare indulgence only.

foods.name: Pav Bhaji
foods.recommendation: Buttered pav and potato bhaji spike carbs. Choose half pav with more bhaji.

foods.name: Bhel Puri
foods.recommendation: Puffed rice snack. Moderate portion as an occasional treat.

foods.name: Pani Puri
foods.recommendation: Fried shells and potato. Enjoy occasionally, limit quantity.

foods.name: Vada Pav
foods.recommendation: Fried potato vada in bread. High carb and fat; rare treat.

foods.name: Dhokla
foods.recommendation: Steamed fermented chickpea cake. Good snack, moderate carbs.

foods.name: Apple
foods.recommendation: Fibre-rich, low GI fruit. Eat whole, not juiced, for slower absorption.

foods.name: Banana
foods.recommendation: Good potassium source but moderately sweet. Choose slightly green bananas.

foods.name: Orange
foods.recommendation: Vitamin C rich, low GI fruit. Great whole-fruit snack.

foods.name: Papaya
foods.recommendation: Digestive-friendly fruit. Moderate portion is blood-sugar safe.

foods.name: Guava
foods.recommendation: High fibre and vitamin C, low GI. Excellent diabetic fruit.

foods.name: Watermelon
foods.recommendation: High water content but high GI. Keep to small servings.

foods.name: Mango
foods.recommendation: Sweet tropical fruit. Enjoy a few slices, not a whole mango.

foods.name: Pomegranate
foods.recommendation: Antioxidant rich with moderate GI. Sprinkle over salads or curd.

foods.name: Pineapple
foods.recommendation: Sweet and tangy, moderate GI. Limit to a small bowl.

foods.name: Grapes
foods.recommendation: Small fruits easy to overeat. Count 15-20 grapes as a serving.

foods.name: Tomato
foods.recommendation: Very low carb, lycopene-rich. Eat freely in salads and curries.

foods.name: Potato
foods.recommendation: High GI root vegetable. Boil and cool before eating to lower impact.

foods.name: Onion
foods.recommendation: Low-calorie flavour base. Safe to include in most dishes.

foods.name: Carrot
foods.recommendation: Beta-carotene rich, low GI. Great crunchy snack.

foods.name: Beans
foods.recommendation: High fibre, low carb. Excellent addition to any meal.

foods.name: Capsicum
foods.recommendation: Vitamin C powerhouse, very low carb. Eat generously.

foods.name: Spinach
foods.recommendation: Iron and folate rich with negligible carbs. Eat freely.

foods.name: Peas
foods.recommendation: Green peas add protein and fibre. Use moderate portions.

foods.name: Cucumber
foods.recommendation: Hydrating and near-zero carb. Perfect snack or salad base.

foods.name: Brinjal
foods.recommendation: Eggplant is low carb and fibre-rich. Great for weight and sugar control.

foods.name: Milk
foods.recommendation: Good calcium source, low GI. Choose toned milk to reduce fat.

foods.name: Curd
foods.recommendation: Probiotic-rich, low GI. Great with meals to slow carb absorption.

foods.name: Paneer
foods.recommendation: High protein, negligible carbs. Excellent for diabetic meals.

foods.name: Buttermilk
foods.recommendation: Hydrating, probiotic-rich, low calorie. Perfect summer drink.

foods.name: Boiled Egg
foods.recommendation: Zero-carb protein source. Excellent for blood sugar stability.

foods.name: Omelette
foods.recommendation: Protein-rich breakfast. Add veggies for fibre and satiety.

foods.name: Chicken Curry
foods.recommendation: High protein, moderate fat. Pair with roti and salad for balance.

foods.name: Fish Curry
foods.recommendation: Omega-3 rich, low carb. Excellent diabetic-friendly protein.

foods.name: Peanuts
foods.recommendation: Healthy fats and protein, low GI. Great snack in small handfuls.

foods.name: Sprouts
foods.recommendation: Nutrient-dense, high protein and fibre. Superfood for diabetics.

foods.name: Aloo Tikki
foods.recommendation: Potato-based snack is high in carbs. If it is fried, skip the chutney to limit sugar; keep it to one tikki.

foods.name: Basundi
foods.recommendation: Sweetened milk dessert. High in sugar and calories; treat as a rare indulgence.

foods.name: Butter Chicken
foods.recommendation: Cream and butter raise fat and calories. Enjoy in small portions with multigrain roti.

foods.name: Chana Masala
foods.recommendation: Chickpea curry is rich in fibre and protein with a low glycemic load. Pair with roti, not rice.

foods.name: Chicken Tikka
foods.recommendation: Tandoori chicken is high in protein and low in carbs. Skip sweet mint chutney to save sugar.

foods.name: Chikki
foods.recommendation: Peanut-jaggery brittle is calorie-dense. Restrict to a small square as an occasional treat.

foods.name: Gajar Ka Halwa
foods.recommendation: Carrot pudding loaded with mawa and ghee. High calorie and sugar; enjoy in tiny servings.

foods.name: Gulab Jamun
foods.recommendation: Deep-fried in sugar syrup. Very high in carbs and sugar; limit to one piece.

foods.name: Jalebi
foods.recommendation: Fermented batter in heavy sugar syrup. Spikes blood sugar; treat as an occasional indulgence.

foods.name: Kadai Paneer
foods.recommendation: Paneer with capsicum and tomato base. High in protein and fat; go light on any butter.

foods.name: Lassi
foods.recommendation: Yogurt drink. Unsweetened lassi is blood-sugar friendly; skip added sugar.

foods.name: Litti Chokha
foods.recommendation: Whole-wheat litti with roasted eggplant chokha. Balanced fibre and protein; keep ghee topping minimal.

foods.name: Ras Malai
foods.recommendation: Cheese dumplings in sweet milk. High sugar; limit to one piece.

foods.name: Sheera
foods.recommendation: Semolina cooked in ghee and sugar. High calories and carbs; occasional treat only.

foods.name: Shrikhand
foods.recommendation: Hung-curd dessert that is high in sugar. Choose plain curd with fruit instead for daily meals.

foods.name: Sohan Papdi
foods.recommendation: Gram-flour brittle made with ghee and sugar. Very sweet; restrict to tiny portions.

foods.name: Unni Appam
foods.recommendation: Banana-jaggery snack, mostly carbohydrate. Keep to one piece as a rare treat.

foods.name: Adhirasam
foods.recommendation: Traditional jaggery & rice sweet. High glycemic impact; strictly limit to half or one piece on special occasions.

foods.name: Aloo Matar
foods.recommendation: Potato and green pea curry. Green peas add beneficial dietary fiber; pair with whole-wheat roti to control glucose spike.

foods.name: Aloo Methi
foods.recommendation: Fenugreek (methi) greens have clinically proven anti-hyperglycemic properties that help offset the potato starch.

foods.name: Aloo Shimla Mirch
foods.recommendation: Bell pepper adds vitamin C and antioxidants with low carbs. Excellent everyday vegetable when cooked with minimal oil.

foods.name: Anarsa
foods.recommendation: Sesame & rice pastry. High carbohydrate density; consume with protein or after physical activity.

foods.name: Ariselu
foods.recommendation: Fried rice flour & jaggery cake. High caloric and carb density; reserve for festive treats in moderation.

foods.name: Bandar Laddu
foods.recommendation: Gram flour sweet cooked in ghee. High sugar and fat content; pair with a fiber-rich meal if eaten.

foods.name: Bhindi Masala
foods.recommendation: Okra (bhindi) is rich in soluble mucilage fiber that delays carbohydrate absorption. Highly recommended for diabetes.

foods.name: Boondi
foods.recommendation: Deep-fried chickpea flour pearls. High fat content; prefer using in cucumber raita to blunt glucose response.

foods.name: Chak Hao Kheer
foods.recommendation: Manipur black rice pudding. Anthocyanin antioxidants in black rice offer lower GI than standard white rice kheer.

foods.name: Cham Cham
foods.recommendation: Chenna sweet dipped in sugar syrup. Squeeze out excess syrup before consuming to reduce carb load by 30%.

foods.name: Chhena Kheeri
foods.recommendation: Odisha paneer/chenna dessert. Cottage cheese protein helps stabilize sugar absorption compared to starch sweets.

foods.name: Chicken Razala
foods.recommendation: Yogurt and cashew based chicken curry. High protein, very low carbohydrate content; excellent for stable glycemic control.

foods.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
foods.recommendation: Rich tandoori chicken in tomato-cream gravy. Very low carbs with high satiety; pair with cucumber salad or 1 roti.

foods.name: Daal Baati Churma
foods.recommendation: Rajasthani classic rich in whole wheat and lentils. High caloric and carb density; monitor portion size carefully.

foods.name: Daal Puri
foods.recommendation: Spiced lentil-stuffed fried bread. Protein from dal moderates glucose spike compared to plain maida puris.

foods.name: Dharwad Pedha
foods.recommendation: Caramelized milk solids sweet. High concentrated sugar; best restricted or consumed in single portion.

foods.name: Doodhpak
foods.recommendation: Semi-thickened milk and rice sweet with saffron and almonds. Nut fats slightly slow postprandial spike.

foods.name: Double Ka Meetha
foods.recommendation: Hyderabadi fried bread pudding in condensed milk and sugar syrup. High glycemic index; caution advised.

foods.name: Dum Aloo
foods.recommendation: Baby potatoes in spiced yogurt or tomato gravy. Consume with high-fiber salad to balance the starch load.

foods.name: Gavvalu
foods.recommendation: Crisp shell-shaped jaggery sweet. High carbohydrate content; limit serving to 1-2 small pieces.

foods.name: Ghevar
foods.recommendation: Honeycomb festive dessert soaked in sugar syrup with rabri. Very high carb & fat density; strictly limit portion.

foods.name: Imarti
foods.recommendation: Urad dal flour spiral soaked in saffron sugar syrup. Higher protein than jalebi, but sugar syrup elevates GI.

foods.name: Kadhi Pakoda
foods.recommendation: Besan and fermented yogurt curry with pakodas. Lactic acid from yogurt provides favorable glycemic regulation.

foods.name: Kajjikaya
foods.recommendation: Coconut and dry fruit stuffed pastry. High fat and carbs; eat half portion to avoid glucose excursion.

foods.name: Kakinada Khaja
foods.recommendation: Layered pastry filled with sugar syrup. Rapidly absorbed sugars; avoid during active hyperglycemia.

foods.name: Kalakand
foods.recommendation: Milk cake made from paneer and condensed milk. Good protein content blunts blood sugar rise relative to pure sugar sweets.

foods.name: Karela Bharta
foods.recommendation: Bitter gourd contains charantin and polypeptide-p, renowned clinical insulin-mimetic agents. Superb for diabetes.

foods.name: Kofta
foods.recommendation: Vegetable or paneer dumplings in spiced gravy. Moderate carbs; pair with whole grains or steamed brown rice.

foods.name: Kuzhi Paniyaram
foods.recommendation: Fermented rice and black gram batter dumplings. Fermentation aids gut microbiome; enjoy with sambar.

foods.name: Ledikeni
foods.recommendation: Bengali fried cottage cheese sweet in syrup. Squeeze out syrup to significantly drop sugar content.

foods.name: Lyangcha
foods.recommendation: Elongated mawa and flour sweet. High sugar density; treat as an occasional festive luxury in moderation.

foods.name: Maach Jhol
foods.recommendation: Traditional Bengali fish curry with mustard & cumin. Exceptional lean protein and Omega-3s with near-zero carbs.

foods.name: Makki Di Roti Sarson Da Saag
foods.recommendation: Mustard greens provide dense dietary fiber, iron, and glucosinolates that naturally blunt the corn flour carbs.

foods.name: Malapua
foods.recommendation: Fried sweet pancake soaked in syrup. High sugar and fat density; recommend eating a quarter or half piece.

foods.name: Misi Roti
foods.recommendation: Chickpea flour (besan) and wheat blend. Superior protein and lower GI than plain chapati; great diabetic choice.

foods.name: Misti Doi
foods.recommendation: Sweetened fermented yogurt. Probiotic benefits are preserved, but contains refined sugar. Enjoy in small cup.

foods.name: Modak
foods.recommendation: Steamed modak with coconut & jaggery has lower fat than fried versions. Coconut fiber moderates sugar surge.

foods.name: Mysore Pak
foods.recommendation: Rich ghee, besan and sugar confection. Very high energy density; consume in minimal moderation.

foods.name: Navrattan Korma
foods.recommendation: Nine vegetables and nuts in mild creamy sauce. Diverse vegetable fibers combined with healthy nut fats.

foods.name: Phirni
foods.recommendation: Ground rice pudding served in earthen matkas. Saffron and cardamom add flavor; share portion to keep carbs under 15g.

foods.name: Pithe
foods.recommendation: Bengali rice flour dumplings with coconut or kheer filling. Steamed versions are much healthier than fried.

foods.name: Poornalu
foods.recommendation: Lentil & jaggery sweet fritter from Andhra. Chana dal provides beneficial protein that lowers glycemic surge.

foods.name: Pootharekulu
foods.recommendation: Paper-thin rice starch roll with sugar/jaggery and dry fruit. Very fast carbohydrate absorption; restrict portion.

foods.name: Qubani Ka Meetha
foods.recommendation: Hyderabadi stewed apricot dessert. Apricots provide dietary fiber, potassium, and vitamins; skip added sugar if homemade.

foods.name: Rabri
foods.recommendation: Condensed milk cream layers. Substantial dairy protein and fats slow digestion, resulting in lower GI than starch sweets.

foods.name: Rasgulla
foods.recommendation: Spongy cottage cheese ball. Squeezing out the sugar syrup thoroughly reduces carbohydrate content by roughly 40%.

foods.name: Sandesh
foods.recommendation: Fresh chenna (paneer) confection. One of the best Indian dessert options for diabetics due to low carbs and high protein.

foods.name: Shankarpali
foods.recommendation: Crispy sweet snack bites. Highly snackable; measure out portion into a small cup rather than eating from container.

foods.name: Sheer Korma
foods.recommendation: Vermicelli and dry-fruit milk pudding. Nuts and whole milk mitigate sharp glycemic peaks.

foods.name: Sohan Halwa
foods.recommendation: Dense wheat flour and dry fruit halwa in pure ghee. High calorie and carb payload; split with a partner.

foods.name: Sutar Feni
foods.recommendation: Shredded dough pastry flavored with cardamom and pistachio. Light texture can be deceptive; high sugar content.
